page.layout: One page of text, with two marginal notes in the right margin: "Lectio 3a." beside the heading "VERSVS XV." and "19. Decemb." beside the first line of the verse. Running head at the top with the page number on the right. Catchword "cibus" at the lower right.

main_text.p: 5. Postremò ἐπιχαιρεκακίας[?] hostilis descriptionem, ultimo loco additam, explicare licebit verbis Dauidis, quae exstant in Psal. 10.8. Sedet in infidiis vicorum: in latebris occidit innocentem: oculi eius in pauperem intenti sunt. 9. Insidiatur in abscondito, sicut leo in spelunca: insidiatur ad abripiendum pauperem: (discerpit) pauperem attrahens eum in rete suo. 10. Deiicit & deprimit se, & cadit in vires eius congregatio pauperum.

Decimum hoc Dei μεγαλέου[?], saepe repetitum, fuit: Hostium populi Dei φόβος ἀντιμόνιος[?], ut eum vocat Pindarus: & eorum, suisipsorum gladijs se invicem conficientium, tragica internecio. Eo enim facto demonstrauit Dominus, longè alio loco apud se esse populum selectum, & verè eximium ποίημα[?]: alio Ethnicos, idololatras, Dei in mundo expertes: ut de illis alicubi pronunciauit diuinus Apostolus.
main_text.head: VERSVS XV.

p.i: Incedere fecisti in mari equos tuos per 19. Decemb. introitum aquarum multarum.

main_text.p: Populum Dei in mediis imperiorum confusionibus, & rerum humanarum vi-

page.notes: The stray mark "y" at the lower left, beside the catchword "cibus", is not printed text and was left out. The Greek words "ἐπιχαιρεκακίας", "μεγαλέου", "ἀντιμόνιος" and "ποίημα" are doubtful and are marked [?]. The note "Lectio 3a." is doubtful and is marked [?]. The spelling "medijs" was normalised to "mediis" because the j is a printed vowel i. "fuisipsorum" and "suisipsorum" were read from a faint scan; the doubtful reading is "suisipsorum". The ligatures "ct" and "st" were expanded to "facto", "demonstrauit" and "selectum".
